posts.title: “forcing/learning to live/love the role” – Nayana Nair
posts.description: . often the only role left to pick was of “the one who wrote to the night”. not a scholar, a poet, or a heart in love; but a port, a branch, a fountain dead. this you become not by your choosing, but by losing everything else. a decision no longer cruel, a circumstance hand-designed. the wanting of those hands, often not about you, but often it was. to grow as no on else, all this fate, all that we have been led to, cause life won’t lead us anywhere else. an unfamiliar happiness often knocks, scares our doors, waits till some moon or some song lights it weary way to a better life. and who could refuse better, though we often have, always will, slowly learning to do so with all our heart. owning the last role left, as all we want. for now the port, and the branch, and the water dead, call to us with all their quiet beauty and love. sometimes a sadness rages in us, the ache of all the loss and denial never quietened by the night storms and morning rains that sing back to us. sometimes a

posts.title: “Hungry Blue Floor” – Nayana Nair
posts.description: . The sea would enter our home and we would sit there, scrapping away the world from each other’s skin. All good advice and better ways lost to the waves. All our stories fed to the hungry blue floor. Worse and light, armed with feelings that have lost all their threads and anchors, we follow some wind whose old betrayal we remember no more. We carve out in tears, some innocence from our old flesh. Our new skin, our old fate lost in a new dance, feet moving to songs that have grown stale in every mouth but ours. In a moon-eaten dress, I walk the aisle to my own ghost, feeling nauseous with the vows, every step sinking into a field of rot.

posts.title: “The Nameless” – Nayana Nair
posts.description: . In the far away, in the too late, in the place I come from, in the place where I have died, wires and veins melt in the summer heat, fishes of soil, die in water averse to hunger, unconsumable by greed. An uncontainable sorrow gives birth on street, numerous hollow wants for taking, the skin of faith waiting for new eyes to see. The postmen with hands of metal, holders like me, walk on forever, with their leaking letters, with gaping hole, the unending shriek, the waking now walking alone, the waking gone to sleep, they walk forever, hiding the ink, till a bullet ends them, saves them, graves them in the coffin of false words, for their crime of distribution, their hand in the tricks of restlessness. The homes and hearts are clean from hope, the infestation of better and unreal always on roll.
